title.en: State the basic postulates and laws of Boolean algebra

say.en: In 1854 George Boole wrote an algebra of true and false. Nearly a century later, Claude Shannon showed it describes switching circuits perfectly. In this lesson: State the basic postulates and laws of Boolean algebra.
Simplify expressions using these laws.

body.en: *Boolean* variables take only 0 or 1. Basic rules: $A + 0 = A$, $A + 1 = 1$, $A\cdot 0 = 0$, $A\cdot 1 = A$, $A + A = A$, $A\cdot A = A$, $A + \overline{A} = 1$, $A\cdot\overline{A} = 0$, and $\overline{\overline{A}} = A$. Commutative: $A + B = B + A$, $AB = BA$. Associative: $(A+B)+C = A+(B+C)$. Distributive: $A(B + C) = AB + AC$ and $A + BC = (A + B)(A + C)$.

points.en: Idempotent: A + A = A, A·A = A
Complement: A + A̅ = 1, A·A̅ = 0; involution A̿ = A

narration.en: Boolean algebra has simple rules: A plus one is one, A times zero is zero, A plus A is A, and A plus not A is one.
narration.kn: ಬೂಲಿಯನ್ ಬೀಜಗಣಿತದ ನಿಯಮಗಳು ಸರಳ: A + 1 = 1, A·0 = 0, A + A = A, ಮತ್ತು A + A̅ = 1.

say.en: Boolean algebra has simple rules: A plus one is one, A times zero is zero, A plus A is A, and A plus not A is one. Identity: A plus 0 equals A, A 1 equals A.
say.kn: ಬೂಲಿಯನ್ ಬೀಜಗಣಿತದ ನಿಯಮಗಳು ಸರಳ: A plus 1 equals 1, A 0 equals 0, A plus A equals A, ಮತ್ತು A plus A̅ = 1.

say.en: Null: A plus 1 equals 1, A 0 equals 0.
Idempotent: A plus A equals A, A A equals A.
Complement: A plus A̅ = 1, A A̅ = 0; involution A̿ = A.
A Boolean variable is only 0 or 1. These basic rules follow from the AND and OR tables.
Distributive laws. The second one is new: it has no match in ordinary algebra.
Absorption: A plus A B. Take A common, 1 plus B is 1, so the answer is just A.
Check with a truth table: the last column is exactly the same as column A.
Another useful result: A plus A-bar B equals A plus B. Fewer terms means fewer gates.
On the board: Boolean laws.

body.en: *Absorption*: $A + AB = A$ and $A(A + B) = A$. Two very useful results: $A + \overline{A}B = A + B$ and $A(\overline{A} + B) = AB$. Every law has a dual, obtained by swapping + with · and 0 with 1. Simplifying an expression reduces the number of gates needed to build it.

narration.en: Absorption removes extra terms: A plus A B is just A. And A plus not A B becomes A plus B. Fewer terms mean fewer gates.
narration.kn: ಹೀರಿಕೆ ನಿಯಮ ಹೆಚ್ಚುವರಿ ಪದಗಳನ್ನು ತೆಗೆಯುತ್ತದೆ: A + AB = A. ಮತ್ತು A + A̅B = A + B. ಕಡಿಮೆ ಪದಗಳು ಎಂದರೆ ಕಡಿಮೆ ದ್ವಾರಗಳು.

say.en: Absorption removes extra terms: A plus A B is just A. And A plus not A B becomes A plus B. Fewer terms mean fewer gates. A plus AB equals A.

steps.en: AB + AB̅ = A(B + B̅) = A·1 = A.
Using A + A̅B = A + B: Y = A + B.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. Simplify Y = AB + AB̅ + A̅B.

say.en: Let us work this out together. Simplify Y equals AB plus AB̅ plus A̅B.
AB plus AB̅ = A(B plus B̅) equals A 1 equals A.
So Y equals A plus A̅B.
Using A plus A̅B equals A plus B: Y equals A plus B.
So the answer is Y equals A plus B one OR gate.

steps.en: Expand the right side: AA + AC + AB + BC.
AA = A, so it is A + AC + AB + BC = A(1 + C + B) + BC.
1 + C + B = 1, so it equals A + BC.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. Prove A + BC = (A + B)(A + C).

say.en: Let us work this out together. Prove A plus BC equals A plus BA plus C.
Expand the right side: AA plus AC plus AB plus BC.
AA equals A, so it is A plus AC plus AB plus BC equals A1 plus C plus B plus BC.
1 plus C plus B equals 1, so it equals A plus BC.
So the answer is Both sides are equal distributive law.
